title: Redwood discovery - reliability & multi-region fallbacks with Sable Retail

Action items include sending SOC2/KMS docs, pricing for Dedicated capacity, and scheduling a technical deep dive and benchmark pilot.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Maya Thompson, Ravi Gupta, Lena Ortiz (Sable Retail)

Summary: quick discovery on reliability/incident tolerance, multi-region fallbacks and what a pilot looks like.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood, I'm the account lead here. Priya, our SE, is on the call. How are you all?
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Hi Alex, hi Priya. Good, thanks. We have a bunch of folks on from infra and ML. Quick context: we're rolling out a recommendations + chat assistant in production across NA and EU and need to understand how Redwood handles outages and cross-region failover.
[00:29] Alex Chen: Great, that's exactly what we want to cover. Quick agenda, we can run through current stack, traffic patterns, desired SLOs, then walk through fallback and routing options and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:40] Ravi Gupta: Sounds good.
[00:42] Lena Ortiz: Yep.
[00:45] Priya Nair: I'll jump in on technical tradeoffs, especially host vs dedicated vs private.
[00:50] Maya Thompson: We're mainly interested in Hosted for speed of integration but need predictable latency and clear incident policies; Dedicated is interesting for P95 and isolation, and Private is a maybe depending on compliance.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Understood. Can you share current numbers — p50/p95 for your inference calls and percent of traffic that's real-time vs batch?
[01:14] Ravi Gupta: Right now our in-house endpoint averages p50 70ms, p95 ~260ms for short sessions, peak qps ~1500 across regions, roughly 60% NA 35% EU 5% APAC. We need sub-200ms p95 for the chat flows or business says it's a hard constraint.
[01:35] Maya Thompson: Also, offline ranking jobs are separate; this is about the 1:1 user-facing requests hitting K8s endpoints.
[01:42] Priya Nair: Thanks, that's helpful. For Hosted we typically see comparable latency to self-hosted for many models, but the guarantees differ. Our Dedicated pools give you SLA-backed throughput and better isolation, and Private gives you full control for compliance.
[01:59] Alex Chen: For reliability, we have multi-region routing with health checks + priority routing. The basic pattern is: primary region serves traffic; upon degraded health or capacity constraints we route to a secondary region with a compatible model variant. We also support model variant fallbacks — e.g. full model -> quantized or distilled variant if compute constrained, with very short switch-over times.
[02:25] Maya Thompson: How fast is the switchover? We ran into problems last quarter when EU infra had a 7-minute outage and our user-facing API errors spiked.
[02:33] Priya Nair: Route decisions are near-real-time; health checks run on short intervals and you can configure SLO-based thresholds. Typical route propagation and warm-up for a variant is within 30-120s depending on KV cache warmup. There is always a brief window where latency may spike while caches fill.
[02:52] Ravi Gupta: KV cache warmup — that's the prefix caching of conversation state right? If we route to another region, do you have cross-region cache warmers or do we accept the cold state?
[03:03] Priya Nair: Good question. We have options: for critical flows you can enable synchronous replication of small KV state to a standby region (added cost). Alternatively we use on-demand prefix warming where the first few requests are slower but then warm. For conversational use-cases we recommend either lightweight KV replication for the last N-turns or pre-warming based on user session affinity.
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: Cost is a concern — synchronous replication sounds pricey. We need to see unit economics for that.
[03:31] Alex Chen: Absolutely — we'll include cost delta in the Dedicated pricing pack. Also, fallback to quantized/dense smaller model can reduce compute cost while keeping service continuity. That is our common pattern: region fallback -> model variant fallback -> graceful degrade (e.g., reduced token length).
[03:50] Maya Thompson: If we fall back to a smaller model, do you see hallucination or quality regressions, and can we set thresholds to notify us?
[03:58] Priya Nair: Yes, quality delta depends on model families and prompt design. We offer regression alerting tied to test prompt sets; you can set a threshold on semantic similarity or business KPIs to trigger an alert and optionally fail open/fail closed.
[04:14] Ravi Gupta: Ok. On SLA, what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:20] Alex Chen: Hosted does not have hard SLA for latency in the self-serve tier; we publish performance profiles and typical p95 ranges. For Dedicated, our contract includes uptime SLA (e.g., 99.9% for endpoint availability) and latency SLOs can be part of the contract with performance credits for breaches. Private deployments are contractually flexible but depend on customer infra.
[04:41] Maya Thompson: 99.9% is reasonable. Do you provide post-incident reports and playbooks?
[04:46] Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated and Private customers we provide incident postmortems, audit logs, and a runbook for failover scenarios. Hosted customers get status updates and incident summaries.
[04:58] Maya Thompson: For security and data residency we need SOC2, KMS support, and SSO. Also, tokens and logs must not leave our EU project region for certain PII flows.
[05:11] Alex Chen: We support KMS integrations and SSO. For data residency you can pin regions and use Private or Dedicated in-region deployments to ensure logs and data stay in-region. We'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs after the call.
[05:24] Lena Ortiz: Good. Regarding testing — we'd like a tailored bench that includes a failover event in the middle of a 48-hour run. Can Redwood simulate cross-region outage and measure client-side error rates and failover latency?
[05:36] Priya Nair: Yes, we can orchestrate a controlled failover during the pilot; we provide test harness and can run synthetic traffic at your requested distributions. We'll capture p50/p95, error rate, and failover time.
[05:48] Ravi Gupta: How do you do routing policy? Weighted traffic, or policy-based on latency/cost/region?
[05:53] Alex Chen: You can configure policies: region affinity, cost-first (route to cheaper region/model), latency-first (route to lowest latency), or custom priority lists. We also support automatic fallback policies when capacity thresholds are hit.
[06:05] Maya Thompson: Does Redwood support canary and A/B rollouts for model changes across regions? We want to test new ranking models on 5% of traffic in EU first.
[06:13] Priya Nair: Yes, the Console supports per-route rollouts — canary, A/B, weighted, and automatic rollback based on latency or quality regressions. This works across regions.
[06:24] Alex Chen: Any regulatory red flags we should know about?
[06:27] Lena Ortiz: We're fine but the payments team is sensitive to any cross-border data movement for transaction metadata. We'll likely ask for Dedicated capacity in-region for those flows.
[06:37] Ravi Gupta: Also wondering about observability — token-level cost, tracing of requests across the routing boundary, and per-model dashboards.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Console gives token-level cost, latency breakdown per step, per-route traces, and error analytics. We can grant read-only views to your SREs.
[06:53] Maya Thompson: Great. A few other questions: 1) If a region is overloaded, do you queue requests or shed load? 2) How do you handle warm restarts to avoid cold-start spikes?
[07:06] Priya Nair: We support graceful degradation: queueing with configurable timeouts, and shedding based on priority. For restarts we have pre-warming and instant warm pool options on Dedicated. On Hosted, there are shared pools and warm-up times are typically short but nonzero.
[07:22] Alex Chen: To summarize the fallback ladder we recommend: 1) local retry -> 2) route to standby region (same model) -> 3) route to quantized/distilled variant in same or different region -> 4) apply graceful degrade (shorter response) -> 5) return a friendly message when critical failure.
[07:41] Ravi Gupta: That helps. Can you give an example timeline for an incident?
[07:45] Priya Nair: Sure — detection in ~30s, route change in 30-90s, cache warm-up 30-120s; so full continuity with transient latency spikes can happen within 2-4 minutes depending on options chosen. If you enable synchronous KV replication it cuts user-state cold window to a few seconds but with cost.
[08:03] Maya Thompson: We need that spelled out in the pilot and in the SLA.
[08:07] Alex Chen: Will do.
[08:10] [10:15 trimmed section — small asides about pricing tiers and contract language]
[10:30] Maya Thompson: On the compliance side, we'll want to see redacted runbooks and the incident postmortem template.
[10:36] Alex Chen: We'll include those.
[10:40] Priya Nair: For the bench, we'll want a sample of your traffic profile, target SLOs, and a list of prompts that represent the business-critical flows so we can include quality regression checks.
[10:52] Ravi Gupta: We'll pull together a dataset.
[11:00] Maya Thompson: How do you charge for multi-region Dedicated pools? Is it per region or a single commitment with regional burst?
[11:08] Alex Chen: Typically per-region reservation for Dedicated; we offer burst capacity and cross-region pooling as an add-on. We'll include pricing scenarios in the deck.
[11:18] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Any concerns about vendor lock-in — if we start with Hosted and later move to Dedicated/Private?
[11:25] Priya Nair: We designed the API and deployment abstractions to be consistent. Customers commonly start Hosted and then reserve Dedicated; model artifacts and prompts move with you. Private is more effort but possible with tooling we provide.
[11:38] Ravi Gupta: One more: will you provide SLA credits if failover triggers? How do you measure incident windows?
[11:44] Alex Chen: SLA credits are measured against contracted endpoint availability metrics and we use our monitoring/trace data to determine windows. We'll put exact language in the contract.
[11:54] Maya Thompson: Thanks. From our side, next steps are security docs, bench plan, pricing, and a deep-dive.
[12:02] Alex Chen: Great. We'll send the SOC2/KMS pack and Draft pricing today or tomorrow, Priya will follow up to schedule the SE deep dive.
[12:10] [Longer sections: deeper technical clarifications]
[20:35] Priya Nair: If you want specific numbers: with Dedicated we can guarantee sustained 2K qps pool with p95 ~<180ms for the model variants we've validated, assuming expected sequence lengths. Distillation/quantization gives different profiles — we'll annotate them.
[22:05] Ravi Gupta: Sequence length on our side is typically 60-120 tokens for recommendations, and 150-400 for the chat assistant. Does Redwood measure per-token cost per region?
[22:18] Priya Nair: Yes, token-level cost by model variant and region. We'll include a cost table.
[28:40] Maya Thompson: How do you authenticate service-to-service? Any fine-grained RBAC for routes?
[28:47] Alex Chen: We support API keys, mTLS for Private, and fine-grained RBAC via SSO/SAML integration for Console and route permissions.
[30:02] Lena Ortiz: For the pilot we'll want a 48-hour window with a scheduled failover in the middle and a canary for model upgrade. Can Redwood commit to that schedule?
[30:12] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll propose dates once we get the traffic sample. We'll run the failover at a low-traffic window and capture metrics.
[30:20] Ravi Gupta: Also want a checklist of what Sable needs to provide — keys, traffic, endpoints to hit for latency measurement.
[30:27] Alex Chen: We'll send a pilot checklist and runbook.
[30:30] [Crosstalk and small clarifications — audio glitch noted]
[40:05] Maya Thompson: If we hit a major incident, what's the on-call engagement for Redwood? Do we get a named SLA contact?
[40:13] Alex Chen: For Dedicated we assign an account SRE/CSM with phone escalation. For Hosted self-serve there's our support portal and priority support add-ons.
[40:23] Lena Ortiz: Good.
[40:25] Priya Nair: Quick note on telemetry — we can stream audit logs to your SIEM or push to an S3 bucket in-region for your compliance team.
[40:34] Ravi Gupta: That will help.
[40:36] Maya Thompson: Anything else we should hedge on?
[40:39] Alex Chen: Just that performance and failure profiles vary by model. We'll run validation on your specific prompts in the bench. Also, define the exact success metrics up front: p95 target, max error rate, maximum failover time, and acceptable quality delta.
[40:55] Maya Thompson: We'll draft that and send.
[41:00] Alex Chen: Great. Recap of action items: Alex - send SOC2/KMS/security docs + pricing; Priya - schedule deep-dive and bench plan; Ravi - share traffic sample and prompts; Sable will review pricing and propose windows for the 48-hour pilot.
[41:20] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks Alex and Priya.
[41:24] Alex Chen: Thank you all. We'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with docs.
[41:29] [Meeting ends — final housekeeping chat and small talk omitted]
[51:45] End of recording

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KVM vs KV cache spelled out) and speaker overlaps. Some proper nouns normalized for readability.

Referenced artifacts: Redwood Dedicated pricing deck (link sent in chat), SOC2 and KMS integration docs (to be sent), draft pilot runbook (will be shared).

Recommended follow-up items (as discussed): detailed bench plan, runbook for failover test, pricing scenarios for Dedicated + KV replication, SOC2 + compliance packet, SE deep dive scheduling.
